chapter.title: Partitions
chapter.para: A partition is the unit of isolation: it has its own memory, its own time windows and its own operating mode. This chapter states how partitions are loaded, started, restarted and stopped. The operating modes follow ARINC 653 and are written COLD_START and WARM_START for the initialization modes (INIT_COLD and INIT_WARM in the code).

section.para: JetOS shall give each partition an operating mode, one of IDLE, COLD_START, WARM_START and NORMAL.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The mode tells what the partition may do and what the kernel does with its time.

section.para: JetOS shall start each partition in COLD_START mode when the module starts.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A partition initializes itself before it works normally.

section.para: JetOS shall load the image of a partition from the archive embedded in the kernel into its memory space when the partition starts, copying its loadable segments, clearing the memory that they do not initialize, and taking the entry point from the image.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The code of the partition is part of the kernel image; it must be put in the right place, and a damaged or oversized image must not corrupt anything.

section.para: JetOS shall check the image of a partition and its loadable segments against the memory space of the partition before it copies them.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A damaged or oversized image must not corrupt anything.

section.para: JetOS shall treat an image that cannot be loaded as a partition load error of the partition (see health monitoring).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A module must come up, or fail visibly, with a bad image in one partition.

section.para: JetOS shall, when a partition starts or restarts, give it empty state: the memory of its image as loaded, no processes created, no ports created, the shared area initialized, all its stacks free.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Each start is a fresh one, so that a restart really recovers the partition.

section.para: JetOS shall run the first process of a partition that starts or restarts, the main process, at the entry point of the image, with preemption locked.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The main process creates the other processes and the ports before the partition works normally.

section.para: JetOS shall restart the calling partition in COLD_START or WARM_START mode when the partition requests that mode.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the mode transitions that ARINC 653 allows to a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall stop the processing of the calling partition when the partition requests IDLE mode.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the mode transitions that ARINC 653 allows to a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall start the processes of the calling partition when the partition requests NORMAL mode.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the mode transitions that ARINC 653 allows to a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall refuse with an error a request of a partition for WARM_START mode while its mode is COLD_START, for NORMAL mode while its mode is NORMAL, and for any other mode.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the mode transitions that ARINC 653 allows to a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall, when a partition enters NORMAL mode, release its locked preemption and start the processes that were started during the initialization: an aperiodic process after its delay, a periodic process at the next start of periodic processing of the partition plus its delay, each with its deadline set.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The initialization ends and the application runs at a defined time.

section.para: JetOS shall, while a partition is in IDLE mode, run none of its processes, while its time slots stay assigned to it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: An idle partition must not disturb the schedule of the others.

section.para: JetOS shall record, for each partition, why it started last (normal start, partition restart, restart by the health monitor of the module or of the partition) and give it, with its identifier, period, duration, mode and lock level, as the status of the partition on request.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: An application decides what to recover from the reason of its start.

section.para: JetOS shall let a partition raise the lock level of its preemption (locking it) up to a maximum of 16 levels, a request beyond it being refused with an error, and lower it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Preemption locking is the ARINC 653 means to protect short critical regions of a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall not preempt the current process of a partition by another process of the partition while the lock level of the partition is above 0.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The lock protects a short critical region of the process that holds it.

section.para: JetOS shall make a partition choose the process to run again when its lock level falls to 0.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Preemption locking is the ARINC 653 means to protect short critical regions of a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall not change the lock level of a partition outside NORMAL mode or in the error handler.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Outside NORMAL mode and in the error handler, the partition does not schedule its processes by priority.

section.para: JetOS shall run, if configured, kernel-only partitions without a memory space of their own, for the monitor and for the debugger, as part of the kernel.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These partitions are parts of the kernel's own diagnostics, not applications.
